correctness.rationale: The Binet expansions and sum formulas imply a monic integer order-three recurrence, reducing the gcd to the first three windows. The evaluation matrix determinant is 432, so at all primes >=5 the gcd valuation is min(vp(B),vp(k)). Direct congruences show exact v2=min(v2(k),3) for both sequences. A 3-adic binomial congruence for k divisible by three gives companion valuation v3(k) and Jacobsthal valuation v3(k)-1; for other k, both 3-parts vanish. Independent exact-integer recurrence-based calculation checked 1400 (length,sequence) cases, each taking 12 shifts; code is corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A complete formula for two standard companion sequences closes a natural sliding-square gcd calculation motivated by earlier explicit square-sum research and the 2022 GCD-of-window-squares study. The exact all-prime answer has nontrivial structure: a saturated 2-part, a 3-part differing by one unit of valuation, and length-controlled odd-prime divisibility. It computes an infinite family of natural arithmetical invariants, rather than a bounded test or a substitution exercise.
